paper_title: Adapting Whisper for Regional Dialects Enhancing Public Services for   Vulnerable Populations in the United Kingdom
caption: Difference in average word error rate (WER) from Whisper large-v3 after cumulative automated optimisation steps.
model_annotation: The chart illustrates the difference in average word error rate (WER) from Whisper large-v3 following various optimisation steps, categorized by model type. The horizontal axis displays model names: "NESAC ft model" and "SESHA ft model", each represented by a different color. The vertical axis is labeled "Difference in Average WER from Whisper large," with a linear scale ranging from 0.000 to 0.004, marked with tick labels at 0.000, 0.001, 0.002, and 0.003. The bars corresponding to "NESAC ft model" are colored orange, while the bars for "SESHA ft model" are green. The "NESAC ft model" bars have values that range approximately from 0.000257 to 0.00302, with the tallest bar depicting "Americanisms" exhibiting an approximate value of 0.00302 and the shortest bar displaying "Dates" with a value of approximately 0.000257. The "SESHA ft model" bars have values ranging approximately from 0.00311 to 0.00344, with the tallest bar, "Add Spacing," reaching approximately 0.00344, and the shortest bar, "Remove Spacing," displaying a value near 0.00311. Both sets of bars are arranged vertically, one stacked directly above the other for visual comparison of the difference in WER across the model types. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, or outlining.
